name: symbolic-address-mapping
instr:
Please add piecewise address mapping to `symbolic-symcache` so a cache can describe code that was moved or copied after its debug information was generated. Add `symbolic_symcache::SymCacheConverter::set_address_mappings(&mut self, mappings: &[(std::ops::Range<u64>, u64)]) -> Result<(), symbolic_symcache::Error>` and the unit variant `symbolic_symcache::ErrorKind::InvalidAddressMappings`. Don't add new crates.

Each pair copies a half-open source interval to an equally sized interval starting at the given destination address. Source intervals may overlap, allowing copies of the same code; destination intervals must not overlap. Both intervals must be nonempty and lie within `0..u32::MAX`, with `u32::MAX` allowed as an exclusive end. Reject invalid mappings with `InvalidAddressMappings`, leaving the previous setting intact. A successful call replaces the previous setting; an empty slice disables mapping. The setting applies to all collected data at serialization, regardless of when it was set.

The resulting cache should resolve destination addresses exactly as the original cache resolved the corresponding source addresses, including complete inline call chains and transformed source information. Destinations outside the copied intervals have no source location. For example, `(100..120, 500)` copies source addresses 100 through 119 to 500 through 519, not to 520. Function entry PCs are mapped too: if an entry has several copies, use its lowest destination; if it has none, use
